headline: Approved gate and porch work at 21 Warren Street and black storm windows at 10 Broad Street.
summary: The commission approved changes at 21 Warren Street, 5 Orne Square, 10 Broad Street, 44 Derby Street, and 0 Washington Square. It continued the chimney request at 21 Warren Street, the shutter request at 10 Broad Street, and the solar request at 1A Cambridge Street. It denied the 41 Chestnut Street application without prejudice.
decisions: Approved the 21 Warren Street gate, porch, and railing system, with a lattice modification at the porch base, 4-0.
Continued the chimney portion of the 21 Warren Street application to the October 7 meeting, 4-0.
Approved the 5 Orne Square electric meter application as submitted in the latest mockup, with screening box and conduit color conditions, 5-0.
Continued the 1A Cambridge Street solar application to September 16, 5-0.
Denied the 41 Chestnut Street application without prejudice, 5-0.
Approved black storm windows at 10 Broad Street with a condition that storm and sash colors match, 5-0.
Continued the 10 Broad Street shutter request to the September 16 meeting, 4-0.
Approved the 44 Derby Street foundation application as submitted, 4-0.
Approved the 0 Washington Square display board application with a condition of Park & Recreation Commission approval, 4-0.
Found 3 Cressey Avenue not historically significant, 5-0.
Voted to write a letter of support to the ZBA for relocating 259 Washington St as a means of preservation, 5-0.

plain_text:
SALEM HISTORICAL COMMISSION 
MINUTES 
September 2, 2026 
 
A meeting of the Salem Historical Commission was held on September 2, 2026 at 6:00PM via Zoom 
Virtual Meeting.  Present were Milo Martinez, Robert Peterson, Margarida Raka-Goncalves, Mark 
Meche (Acting Chair), Brendan Murray.  Staff: Patti Kelleher. Absent: Vijay Joyce, Chair Kelly Tyler-
Lewis, Vice Chair Rebecca English, Emily Gonzalez. 
 
Mr. Meche served as Interim Chair in the absences of Chair Tyler-Lewis and Vice Chair English. 
 
 
21 Warren Street–continuation from July 1, 2026 meeting 
Carrie and Lee Dichter applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness for entry and fence design and 
chimney removal.   
 
Mr. Murray recused from discussion of this item. 
 
Architect Helen Sides was present.  These items were continued from an earlier meeting on July 1.  Ms. 
Sides discussed the driveway gate and the porch design including railings and stairs.  Ms. Sides showed a 
survey of proposed 2-story addition where a new platform with stairs and surrounding railing would be 
added (replacing existing stairs to match existing).  The existing porch at the midpoint of the house is in 
disrepair and needs to be replaced.  Photos of neighboring porches of abutters’ homes were shown, 
including a railing system to copy.  Square balusters, simple handrail system, bottom portion would have 
the same skirtboard, simply posts with flat caps, chamfered railings.  Photos were also shown of the type 
of gate to be installed in the driveway.   
 
Mr. Meche clarified that new stairs would emerge from the rear of the property with landing on the first 
floor of the house.  Mr. Peterson called the approach “reasonable” regarding the stairs and railing system.  
Mr. Peterson said that the appearance of the gate mimicked the porch.  Ms. Sides shared the addresses for 
the gate (15 Warren Street) and porch & railing system (19 Warren Street).  The gate would be modified 
extending from one set of stairs to a property line with column posts at each side.  Chair Meche said two 
swinging gate leaves would not have much slack.  Mr. Martinez asked if the porches could or should 
match each other.  Ms. Sides said that the one in disrepair would be rebuilt.  Mr. Martinez preferred lattice 
under the porch instead of vertical board.  Ms. Sides said the applicants were open to lattice.   
 
No public comment. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Peterson motioned to approve the application for the proposed gate across driveway, and the 
porches and railing system as submitted, with modification of using orthogonal lattice at base of porch 
rather than vertical boards; and base also framed with 1-by around the edges.  Mr. Martinez seconded the 
motion.  Roll Call: Raka-Goncalves, Martinez, Peterson, Meche were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
Discussion shifted to the chimney.  The applicants were researching costs of building a faux chimney, 
which was said to be quite substantial, close to $20,000.  A structural engineer would be needed, as 
building a fake chimney was not an insubstantial request.  Mr. Dichter spoke to vantage points from 
which the chimney desired for removal could be seen.  Ms. Raka-Goncalves clarified that the chimney 
towards the rear of the roof was desired to be removed.
Historical Commission meeting minutes September 2, 2026 
Page 2 of 6 
 
VOTE:  Ms. Raka-Goncalves motioned to continue the chimney portion of application to the October 7 
meeting.  Mr. Peterson seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Raka-Goncalves, Martinez, Meche 
were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
 
5 Orne Square–continuation 
Amy Sinatra and Alexander Spina applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness for electric meters.   
 
Ms. Sinatra was present to deliver a new mockup to documents.  The setup would be the same but the 
location of the conduit was moved to be as short as possible and tight to the upper window.  Chair Meche 
reminded the Board that the weatherhead had to be 3 feet away from any window.  Mr. Peterson did not 
see any other possibility as to conduit placement.  Prior to a site visit, Chair Meche had felt that a more 
compact install could occur by leaving the meter in the basement.  Ms. Kelleher questioned if a screening 
box for meter had been considered and showed an example on Federal Court.  Mr. Martinez said that the 
screening box could be painted Essex Green which was the color of the fencing, rather than the body 
color of the house, while the conduit should be painted to match the color of the house. 
 
No public comment. 
 
Ms. Sinatra said goals was to alter the stucco as little as possible rather than affixing something to the 
wall cladding.  Thus a screening cover that sat on the ground and appeared as a landscape feature coming 
out of the ground was desired.   
 
VOTE:  Mr. Martinez motioned to approve the application as submitted in the latest mockup, with the 
request to add a simple box or landscape feature painted Essex Green, mounted in ground, to cover new 
panels, and conduit to be painted shade of beige closely matching the facade of the house.  Ms. Raka-
Goncalves seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Martinez, Murray, Raka-Goncalves, Meche were in 
favor and the motion so carried. 
 
 
1A Cambridge Street–continuation 
Eleanor Uddo applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to install solar.   
 
The applicant requested a continuation to gather more information. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Peterson motioned to continue the application to September 16.  Ms. Raka-Goncalves 
seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Martinez, Murray, Raka-Goncalves, Meche were in favor and 
the motion so carried. 
 
 
41 Chestnut Street–continuation 
Richard Jagolta applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to remove fencing and install EV charger.   
 
The applicant was not present and did not reach out with any updates. 
 
No public comment.
Historical Commission meeting minutes September 2, 2026 
Page 3 of 6 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Peterson motioned to deny the application without prejudice.  Ms. Raka-Goncalves 
seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Martinez, Murray, Raka-Goncalves, Meche were in favor and 
the motion so carried. 
 
 
10 Broad Street 
Brett McCarty applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to replace shutters and storm window color.   
 
Ms. McCarty was present. She noted that the manufacturer would construct storms to be proportionate to 
existing windows.  Shutters were rotted and not reparable and would be replaced.  Shutters and storms 
would be black (whereas existing shutters were grayish blue).  The selected shutter was Truefit PVC All 
Louver Shutters (12”W x 25”H) with S hooks.  Chair Meche questioned if it was appropriate to have 
black storms over white window sash and trim, as did Mr. Martinez.  Mr. Murray noted a neighboring 
house had white storms on white windows. Other houses were shown with black window sash and black 
storm windows. 
 
Ms. McCarty asked if a condition could be added that storm window color match window sash color, i.e.  
black storms to match black sashes and white storms to match white sashes. 
 
No public comment. 
 
VOTE:  Ms. Raka-Goncalves motioned to approve the black storm windows with the condition that 
sashes would match black; or white storm windows to match current white sashes; sash sizes of storms to 
be proportionate to sash sizes of windows; if black, to be high gloss.  Mr. Martinez seconded the motion.  
Roll Call: Peterson, Martinez, Raka-Goncalves, Murray, Meche were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
Mr. Martinez said that requests for shutters were rare and urged caution with non-natural materials.  Ms. 
McCarty offered to procure samples for the Commission.  Mr. Martinez discouraged smooth and shiny 
material.  Mr. Martinez questioned what type of paint would be recommended for manufactured 
materials.  Mr. Martinez advised brush painting the shutters. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Peterson motioned to continue the shutter request to September 16 meeting.  Mr. Murray 
seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Martinez, Raka-Goncalves, Murray, were in favor and the 
motion so carried. 
 
 
44 Derby Street 
Kate Lerner and Adam Liebowitz applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to renovate the foundation.   
 
Mr. Murray recused from discussion. 
 
Mr. Liebowitz uploaded a Google Street view screenshot for review.  The house had been damaged by 
masonry scammers.  A portion of the foundation was repaired previously with a waterstruck brick in 
uniform color; the applicant is now seeking approval to extend that waterstruck brick to the street-facing 
side of the house.  Mr. Peterson and Ms. Raka-Goncalves commended the new work.  Chair Meche noted 
that the applicant had installed a heat pump without notice and approval, requesting that a new after the 
fact application be submitted for this work.
Historical Commission meeting minutes September 2, 2026 
Page 4 of 6 
 
No public comment. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Martinez motioned to accept the application as submitted.  Ms. Raka-Goncalves seconded 
the motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Raka-Goncalves, Martinez, Meche were in favor and the motion so 
carried. 
 
 
0 Washington Square 
Salem Common Neighborhood Association applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to install a 
display board.   
 
Mr. Martinez recused from discussion as the applicant. 
 
Mr. Martinez presented the SCNA’s application for a new sign board on the Common. Looking to have a 
more physical way to engage the community, i.e. 3” fluted post community message board; pineapple-
styled caps/finials; made of cast aluminum.  Install location would be across from O’Donnell Funeral 
Home, to be placed between fence and walkway.  An image of placement was shown - parallel to the 
fence, one-sided.  The message side would face the interior Common walkway.  Ms. Kelleher said that 
SHC was Mr. Martinez’s first step to be followed by review and approval by the Park & Recreation 
Commission.  Ms. Kelleher noted that the Friends of the Common had discussed placing a wayfinding 
sign at the other end of the Common.  Mr. Martinez said that the community board sign was 30” by 36”, 
with a keyed locked glass case.   
 
No public comment. 
 
Ms. Kelleher proposed including a condition that the community message board be approved by Park & 
Recreation Commission. 
 
VOTE:  Ms. Raka-Goncalves motioned to approve the application as submitted with the condition that it 
gets approval from Park & Recreation Commission as well.  Mr. Peterson seconded the motion.  Roll 
Call: Peterson, Murray, Raka-Goncalves, Meche were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
 
3 Cressey Avenue 
Derrek and Shana Coss applied for a Waiver of the Demolition Delay Ordinance to demolish more than 
50% of roof on a house older than 50 years.   
 
SL Haus Group representative Jacob Levine said the building footprint would not be altered at all.  Two 
new bathrooms would be added on the second floor.  Schematic design drawings were shown featuring 
scope of work.  Single family renovation, remove existing roof and dormers, new second floor layout 
including two bathrooms and bedroom, no scope on first floor or basement, existing footprint to remain.  
Mr. Levine said that vinyl siding would be used, and a 1’ overhang would be created.  Ms. Kelleher said 
some Cressey Avenue properties had been inventoried but not 3 Cressey Avenue.  Chair Meche noted the 
construction date of 1955.  Mr. Levine was unable to find historical drawings shedding light on the 
originality of the dormers.  Ms. Raka-Goncalves clarified that the window on the side of the house was 
being lost.  Chair Meche said that proposed two-story house design looked like Garrison Colonial, which 
would have been typical for this period.  Simple pitch awning over the front door would maintain/retain 
existing walkway.  Mr. Peterson called the house a classic Cape Cod, which Mr. Murray agreed with.
Historical Commission meeting minutes September 2, 2026 
Page 5 of 6 
 
 
No public comment. 
 
Mr. Levine said that white vinyl would likely be used on all sides. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Peterson motioned to find the building not historically significant.  Mr. Murray seconded the 
motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Martinez, Murray, Raka-Goncalves, Meche were in favor and the motion so 
carried. 
 
 
8½ Rear Allen Street 
Lacey Smith applied for a waiver of the Demolition Delay Ordinance to demolish more than 50% of roof 
or walls on houses older than 50 years.   
 
Ms. Kelleher reported that the application should not have been advertised since the project proposed 
removal of less than 50% of the building roof or walls.  Mr. Levine nonetheless showed application 
materials.  A variance approval would be sought through Zoning, to add 10’ additions on two sides of the 
building.   
 
 
Other Business 
 
60-62 Washington Sq 
 
Ms. Kelleher received emails and calls from a resident concerned about a fence adjacent to property that 
was falling over.  The fence was originally approved in 2011 and constructed as conditioned.  The fence 
in its current condition does not comply with the original approval.  The caller was also in touch with the 
Building Commissioner. 
 
 
259 Washington St 
 
Property had previously sought WDDO Waiver which was denied.  Zoning changes had occurred in the 
interim.  The owner was considering moving the building to a parcel on Cedar Street.  The owner 
requested SHC support for preservation through relocating.   
 
VOTE:  Mr. Martinez motioned to write a letter of support to ZBA for relocation as means of 
preservation.  Mr. Raka-Goncalves seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Martinez, Murray, Raka-
Goncalves, Meche were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
 
Unveiling of Washington Portrait at City Hall 
 
Ms. Kelleher invited SHC members to attend the unveiling of Washington portrait on Tuesday September 
8, 2026 at 11:00 AM.
Historical Commission meeting minutes September 2, 2026 
Page 6 of 6 
 
Adjournment 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Murray motioned to adjourn.  Mr. Martinez seconded the motion.  All were in favor and the 
motion so carried. 
 
 
The meeting adjourned at 7:58 PM. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
Dan Graham, Historical Commission Clerk
